Help with 3.5 year old wanting to learn about zoology
American Museum Of Natural History has this very entertaining Zoology for children on their website.

One thing you can consider as a resource is a show like "Wild Kratts". They go all around trying solve problems by using "Animal Powers", taking on the attributes of a specific animal, and in the process talk about the different traits that the animal has. It seems to be pretty popular due to the entertainment factor, and I think for a 3.5 year old you should avoid too much of a technical approach. The main thing is to avoid making learning boring.

Another consideration would be a visit to a zoo in your local area, if one is near by. The zoo will probably have some plaques next to the animal enclosures that describe the habitat, diet etc. of each animal. While there she can actually see the animals and you can ask her questions like "what do you think it eats? Why?" "Where do you think it comes from?".

You can also set up a bird feeder. It will attract songbirds which you can look up online, there is probably a good resource available if you search "Songbirds of <Insert your geographic area here>". You could make a game out of watching the birds and recording which ones you have seen.

The children's section of your local library might also have a nice selection of books. It might be worthwhile to go there with her and help her look around. If you are both there then she can pick a book that looks interesting to her, the fact that she picked it might increase the chances of it being good for her level.
